page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, this server provides a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It features dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute performance without resource sharing or burstable degradation.

This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached block storage. Additionally, the configuration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware profile is designed for workloads that require substantial parallel processing capabilities and a balanced memory footprint without the need for local NVMe drives or hardware-based graphics acceleration.

From a resource density perspective, the n4d-standard-64 offers a standard general-purpose profile suitable for enterprise applications, web serving fleets, application servers, and moderate database deployments. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance lies in its balanced resource ratio, which prevents over-provisioning of either compute or memory for standard multi-threaded workloads. It is well-suited for containerized microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and general-purpose business applications.

It is suited for applications such as web serving, application servers, container orchestration, and general-purpose business workloads that require significant parallel processing capacity without specialized hardware acceleration.
